title: ROSE: RADICAL Orchestrator for Surrogate Exploration
problem: Surrogate modeling at scale requires managing expensive simulations, dynamic data generation, and tight coupling of simulation-inference-training. Existing workflow systems lack support for active learning, asynchronous execution, and heterogeneous resources.
motivation: Scientific computing increasingly relies on surrogates for acceleration and real-time prediction. Active learning (surrogate-guided data acquisition) requires orchestrating asynchronous workflows across diverse HPC resources with minimal user overhead.
method: ROSE is a framework that coordinates expensive physics simulations and machine learning model training across multiple supercomputers (Polaris, Perlmutter, Delta). Instead of guessing which simulations to run next, it uses active learning—an algorithm that selects new simulations based on what would most improve the model's predictions. The system can run analysis alongside the simulations (in-situ) or afterward (ex-situ), and it updates its predictive model either continuously as new data arrives (online) or in batches (offline). By handling all this coordination asynchronously and adapting which simulations to run based on what it learns, ROSE efficiently builds and refines surrogate models—learned predictors that mimic expensive simulations.
key_novelty: The framework orchestrates active learning (intelligently selecting which simulations to run) and asynchronous parallel execution across multiple supercomputers to manage the entire surrogate modeling pipeline, reducing orchestration overhead.
contributions: ROSE framework for surrogate modeling lifecycle management
Active learning algorithm integration with scalable orchestration
Asynchronous execution across heterogeneous HPC resources
Support for in-situ/ex-situ and online/offline workflows
Dynamic adaptive sampling and surrogate refinement
1.5-3× speedup (asynchronous vs synchronous) from pilot-based execution
limitations: Evaluation limited to 3 specific use cases
Comparison with other workflow systems (Parsl, Swift/T) absent
primary_theme: Asynchronous orchestration for surrogate-based scientific computing
